deck.title: EC2 — Elastic Compute Cloud
deck.analogy: EC2 is a rental car agency: the instance family is the car type, the purchasing option is the rental contract.

subtopics.title: Placement groups: where the cars park
ENI: the detachable network identity card
Elastic IP: the phone number you own
Boot-time toolkit: user data, metadata, hibernate

cards.front: What is Amazon EC2, and what two questions do most EC2 exam questions ask?

back.answer: EC2 rents a virtual machine (instance) in AWS. Exam questions ask: which car (family) or which contract (purchasing option)?
back.explanation: You pick size and payment, launch, and get an instance with an IP you can SSH into.
back.mnemonic: EC2 is a rental car agency: family = car type, purchasing option = contract.

cards.front: In the EC2 name m5.2xlarge, what do m, 5 and 2xlarge mean?

back.answer: m = family (what it's good at), 5 = generation, 2xlarge = size (more vCPU and RAM).
back.explanation: Newer generation is better value; bigger size means more vCPU and RAM.

cards.front: EC2 M family: what is it good for?

back.answer: General purpose, balanced CPU:RAM, e.g. web app servers with no special demands.

cards.front: EC2 T family: what is it good for?

back.answer: Burstable instances for spiky, mostly-idle workloads such as dev/test, using CPU credits.

cards.front: EC2 C family: what is it good for?

back.answer: CPU-hungry work: batch processing, encoding, HPC, gaming servers.

cards.front: EC2 R family: what is it good for?

back.answer: Memory-hungry work: in-memory caches and real-time big data analytics.

cards.front: Which EC2 family does the keyword SAP HANA signal?

back.answer: X family: massive in-memory databases.
back.explanation: The word SAP HANA alone means X family.

cards.front: EC2 I family: what is it good for?

back.answer: Fast local NVMe storage: high random I/O, NoSQL needing local disk.

cards.front: EC2 D family: what is it good for?

back.answer: Lots of local HDD storage: distributed file systems, data warehousing.

cards.front: EC2 P family vs G family vs Inf: which does what?

back.answer: P = GPU for ML training; G = graphics rendering and ML inference; Inf = purpose-built inference chips.
back.explanation: Inf suits cost-effective inference at scale; G suits video rendering and game streaming.
back.mnemonic: P = Power training; G = Graphics; Inf = Inference

cards.front: What does a g suffix (m7g, c7g) mean on an EC2 instance, and what exam signals point to it?

back.answer: Graviton, AWS's own ARM processor. Signals: best price-performance, reduce compute cost, sustainability.
back.explanation: Applies to Linux workloads that can run on ARM.

cards.front: How do EC2 T-family burstable instances use CPU credits?

back.answer: They earn credits while idle and spend them to burst above a small baseline CPU.
back.explanation: Great for workloads that are quiet most of the day.
back.mnemonic: Like a phone battery: charges when idle, drains when busy.

cards.front: A t3 instance ran fine for hours, then degraded under sustained load. Why, and what are the fixes?

back.answer: CPU credits ran out, so it was throttled to baseline. Fix: move to M/C family, or enable T Unlimited mode.
back.explanation: M and C families don't use credits. Unlimited keeps bursting but bills for the overage.

cards.front: After enabling a setting on a T instance, the bill rose during a traffic spike. What is the cause?

back.answer: T Unlimited mode overage charges.
back.explanation: Bursting past credits isn't free — it's a loan.

cards.front: What two words in a question decide the EC2 purchasing option?

back.answer: How long (duration) and how interruptible the workload is.
back.explanation: This is the most-tested pricing topic on the exam.

cards.front: When is EC2 On-Demand the answer?

back.answer: Short-term, unpredictable workloads; anything under 1 year. No discount, no commitment.
back.explanation: RIs and Savings Plans start at 1 year.

cards.front: EC2 Standard Reserved Instances: discount and commitment?

back.answer: Up to 72% off, 1 or 3 year commitment; for steady, predictable 24/7 workloads like databases.

cards.front: EC2 Convertible RI: discount and when to use it?

back.answer: Up to 66% off, 1 or 3 years; for steady load when the instance family might change.
back.explanation: You trade discount for flexibility.

cards.front: What do you commit to with EC2 Savings Plans?

back.answer: A $/hour spend for 1 or 3 years, with discount about the same as RIs and flexibility otherwise.

cards.front: EC2 Spot instances: discount and interruption terms?

back.answer: Up to 90% off, no commitment; AWS can reclaim with a 2-minute warning.
back.explanation: Fits fault-tolerant, stateless, batch, interruptible work.

cards.front: When is an EC2 Dedicated Host the answer?

back.answer: BYOL with per-socket or per-core licensing; you get a whole physical server.

cards.front: When is an EC2 Dedicated Instance the answer?

back.answer: Must not share hardware with other customers, but no license or host visibility needs; cheaper than Host.

cards.front: Which EC2 purchase options reserve capacity in an AZ, and which don't?

back.answer: Zonal RIs and On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve capacity. Regional RIs and Savings Plans are billing-only.
back.explanation: Zonal RI = discount AND a seat reservation.

cards.front: EC2 Compute Savings Plan vs EC2 Instance Savings Plan?

back.answer: Compute: any family, any region, plus Fargate and Lambda, smaller discount. Instance: one family in one region, bigger discount.
back.explanation: Compute keyword: flexibility to change types and regions. Instance keyword: committed to family, largest savings.

cards.front: Which EC2 workloads fit Spot, and which must never use it?

back.answer: Fit: stateless, fault-tolerant, checkpointable, batch work. Never: databases or anything that cannot tolerate interruption.
back.explanation: "Cannot tolerate interruption" disqualifies Spot no matter how much the question stresses cost.

cards.front: Predictable baseline traffic plus unpredictable surges on EC2, minimizing cost: what combo?

back.answer: Reserved Instances or Savings Plan for the baseline, plus Spot (or On-Demand) for the surges.

cards.front: EC2 Dedicated Host vs Dedicated Instance: what's the visibility difference?

back.answer: Host exposes sockets, cores and host ID (needed for per-socket/core BYOL). Instance gives isolation with no physical visibility, and costs less.
back.explanation: "Socket" or "BYOL" in the question means Dedicated Host.

cards.front: What are the three EC2 placement group strategies and their mnemonic?

back.answer: Cluster, Spread, Partition. Cluster = Close, Spread = Solo, Partition = Packs.
back.mnemonic: Cluster = Close, Spread = Solo, Partition = Packs.

cards.sourceHeading: Placement groups: where the cars park

cards.front: EC2 Cluster placement group: characteristics, keywords and risk?

back.answer: Same rack in one AZ; lowest latency, highest throughput. For HPC and tightly-coupled nodes. Risk: rack failure kills all.

cards.sourceHeading: Placement groups: where the cars park

cards.front: EC2 Spread placement group: how does it work and what is its limit?

back.answer: Each instance on its own rack with separate power/network; max 7 instances per AZ. For a few critical instances.

cards.sourceHeading: Placement groups: where the cars park

cards.front: EC2 Partition placement group: structure, scale and keywords?

back.answer: Up to 7 partitions per AZ, each an isolated rack group with hundreds of instances; Hadoop, Cassandra, Kafka, HDFS.
back.explanation: A rack failure hits one partition only, and instances can read their partition from instance metadata.

cards.sourceHeading: Placement groups: where the cars park

cards.front: A critical fleet of 20 EC2 instances must each be isolated from hardware failure. Spread group?

back.answer: Spread caps at 7 per AZ: spread across 3 AZs (7+7+6) or use Partition. Count the instances.

cards.sourceHeading: Placement groups: where the cars park

cards.front: What does an EC2 Elastic Network Interface (ENI) carry?

back.answer: The private IP address, MAC address and security groups — not the instance.
back.explanation: Detach it from a failed instance and attach to a standby, which answers on the same private IP.

cards.sourceHeading: ENI: the detachable network identity card

cards.front: Standby EC2 must take over with the same private IP and no client changes: what's the trick?

back.answer: Move the ENI to the standby instance.

cards.sourceHeading: ENI: the detachable network identity card

cards.front: Can an ENI fail over to an instance in another AZ?

back.answer: No — an ENI lives in one subnet, so it only moves within the same AZ.
back.explanation: Cross-AZ failover needs DNS, a load balancer or Route 53.

cards.sourceHeading: ENI: the detachable network identity card

cards.front: Why attach multiple ENIs to one EC2 instance?

back.answer: Dual-homing, e.g. one interface on the public network and one on a separate management network.

cards.sourceHeading: ENI: the detachable network identity card

cards.front: Clients can't reach an EC2 instance after maintenance stop/start. Why, and what's the fix?

back.answer: The auto-assigned public IP changes on stop/start (it survives reboot). Fix: an Elastic IP.

cards.sourceHeading: Elastic IP: the phone number you own

cards.front: What is an Elastic IP, and how does its remapping differ from an ENI move?

back.answer: A static public IPv4 address you own, remappable to any instance, even across AZs (unlike an ENI).

cards.sourceHeading: Elastic IP: the phone number you own

cards.front: When are Elastic IPs charged, and what is the default limit?

back.answer: Charged when not attached to a running instance; soft limit of 5 per region.

cards.sourceHeading: Elastic IP: the phone number you own

cards.front: Best practice instead of Elastic IPs for a stable EC2 entry point?

back.answer: A load balancer with a DNS name, or Global Accelerator (2 static anycast IPs).

cards.sourceHeading: Elastic IP: the phone number you own

cards.front: When does EC2 user data run and as which user?

back.answer: Once, at first boot, as root.
back.explanation: Keyword: automatically install/configure software at launch.

cards.sourceHeading: Boot-time toolkit: user data, metadata, hibernate

cards.front: What is the EC2 instance metadata URL and what does it expose?

back.answer: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ — instance ID, AZ, IAM role credentials, partition number.

cards.sourceHeading: Boot-time toolkit: user data, metadata, hibernate

cards.front: How does EC2 IMDSv2 differ from v1, and when is it the answer?

back.answer: IMDSv2 requires a session token first (PUT, then use token), blocking SSRF. Answer to "protect metadata from SSRF".

cards.sourceHeading: Boot-time toolkit: user data, metadata, hibernate

cards.front: What does EC2 Hibernate do, and what are its requirements?

back.answer: Writes RAM to the encrypted EBS root volume and restores it on start. Root must be encrypted EBS and RAM must fit.
back.explanation: Keywords: long-running in-memory state, pre-warmed caches, reduced boot time.

cards.sourceHeading: Boot-time toolkit: user data, metadata, hibernate

cards.front: Nightly image batch job on EC2; jobs can be re-run if they fail; minimize cost. Which option?

back.answer: Spot instances.
back.explanation: Fault-tolerant, interruptible and cheapest fits Spot.

choices.why: Re-runnable jobs tolerate interruption at up to 90% off.

cards.front: Critical payment workload on EC2, cannot tolerate interruption, minimize cost. Which option?

back.answer: Reserved Instances or a Savings Plan — not Spot.
back.explanation: "Cannot tolerate interruption" disqualifies Spot.

choices.why: Can be reclaimed with 2 minutes' notice.
Costs more than a commitment for steady load.

cards.front: SAP HANA in-memory database on EC2: which instance family?

back.answer: X family.
back.explanation: Plain in-memory cache/analytics would be R family.

cards.front: Train a deep learning model vs serve ML predictions cheaply on EC2: which families?

back.answer: P family for training; G or Inf for inference.

choices.text: G for training, P for inference
C for training, R for inference
X for training, D for inference
P for training, G or Inf for inference

cards.front: Company has per-socket Windows Server licenses to bring to AWS. Which EC2 option?

back.answer: Dedicated Host.
back.explanation: Sockets/cores/BYOL need Host visibility; mere isolation is Dedicated Instance.

choices.why: Exposes sockets and cores for BYOL.

cards.front: Must guarantee EC2 capacity in a specific AZ for month-end processing. Which option?

back.answer: Zonal Reserved Instance or On-Demand Capacity Reservation.
back.explanation: Savings Plans and regional RIs are billing-only.

cards.front: A t3 instance performs well, then slows dramatically after hours of sustained load. What's the cause and fix?

back.answer: CPU credits exhausted, throttled to baseline — move to M/C family or enable Unlimited mode.
back.explanation: A bill spike after enabling a setting means Unlimited overage.

choices.text: Credits exhausted; use M/C or Unlimited
choices.why: Throttled to baseline once credits run out.

choices.text: Move to a Spread placement group

cards.front: After stopping and starting an EC2 instance, users can't reach the old address. Fix?

back.answer: The public IP changed on stop/start — assign an Elastic IP.
back.explanation: Default public IPs are not sticky.

choices.why: Doesn't give a static public IP.
Static public IPv4 that you own.

cards.front: On primary EC2 failure, standby must take over with the same private IP and no client changes. Solution?

back.answer: Move the ENI to the standby (same AZ only).

choices.text: Move the ENI to the standby
choices.why: ENI carries the private IP; same AZ.
Public IPs aren't the private IP.

choices.text: Use user data on the standby

cards.front: Tightly-coupled HPC workload on EC2 needs the lowest inter-node latency. Which placement?

back.answer: Cluster placement group.
back.explanation: Kafka/Cassandra/Hadoop at scale = Partition; 7 critical solo instances = Spread.

cards.front: Steady $ commitment but freedom to switch families, regions, and even Fargate/Lambda. Which plan?

back.answer: Compute Savings Plan.
back.explanation: One family, one region, max discount = EC2 Instance Savings Plan.

choices.why: Locked to one family and region.
Any family, region, plus Fargate and Lambda.

cards.front: Predictable baseline plus unpredictable spikes on EC2, optimize cost. Best approach?

back.answer: RI/Savings Plan for baseline plus Spot for spikes.
back.explanation: The classic combo.
